newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch stock, options exchanges revive merger plans.
newsitem.headline: Dutch stock, options exchanges revive merger plans.

text.p: Amsterdam's stock and options exchanges said on Friday they planned to merge and form a new joint company to boost their international competitive position.
Preliminary proposals for a merger between the two bourses on an equal footing were given the go-ahead by the exchanges' respective executive councils during separate meetings on Thursday night.
"The councils...yesterday granted a mandate for the further working out of plans presented to them for a merger on the basis of equality," the bourses said in a joint statement.
Detailed merger proposals would be submitted for approval at the end of October, the statement added.
The two bourses have been flirting with the idea of a merger for more than two years, but earlier plans foundered on internal disagreements.
Under the plans, the two exchanges will become operating companies of a new firm, Amsterdam Exchanges, which will acquire all their outstanding shares.
The exchanges' existing members will gain a combined 50 percent holding in the new company in the form of cumulative preference shares.
The remaining 50 percent of shares will be offered to listed companies and institutional investors, the statement added.
The new company will be headed by a four-man executive board comprising a general director and the chairmen of the executive boards of the two bourses and their combined clearing arm.
The board will report to an independent, self-perpetuating supervisory board, the statement added.
